description: Alternative R&B core: dark, moody, sexy, vocal-forward, genre-blending R&B. Loves the artists who crossed lanes (electronic, hiphop, pop) without losing the romance. STRUCTURAL DRAFT — tweak the details.
notes: Focused single-lane profile: the test is subtlety WITHIN alt R&B (who keeps the dark/moody/sexy soul vs playlist-slop R&B-pop), plus one or two clean bridges out of the lane (The Weeknd's electronic side, Frank Ocean's experimental side). Edit freely — the golden set (eval/golden/alt_rnb.json) is the answer key and every entry in it must be inferable from these reviews.

reviews.text: This is what R&B should be. Dark, cinematic, the vocals are up front but the production pulls in all these electronic and hiphop ideas and none of it feels like a genre. Every song feels like a scene. The best album of his by a mile — Before He Catches You alone is a masterpiece

Songs that still wreck me years later. Pyramids and Lost are just perfect — heartbroken, sunny, a little weird, nothing else sounds like it. It's the album I keep coming back to when I want something real instead of another pop record. Everything he's done since orbits this one

Adapt is still one of the best songs of this decade, period. The album is a little all-over the place but the peaks are so high — Adia, Come Through, He Art. It's romantic and a little chaotic and sounds like Miguel actually went and lived in the world instead of writing about it. Not perfect, but the best thing from that whole 2012 R&B wave for me
